item.title: AI and Global Food Security: A Focus on Early Warning Systems
item.description: AI promises to improve food security early warning systems, which help inform decisionmakers and prevent hunger before it arises. CSIS experts unpack the risks and benefits of AI-enabled tools for food security early warning systems around the world.

item.title: The Geopolitics of Maduro’s Capture: What Does Operation Absolute Resolve Mean for Russia?
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Associate Fellow Henry Ziemer assesses the implications of the recent U.S. capture of Nicolás Maduro for Russia's strategy in the Western Hemisphere.

item.title: Exploring the New Math Puzzle of a PJM Intervention
item.description: The White House NEDC and partnering agencies released a Statement of Principles to urge PJM to make electricity more affordable for residential customers and strengthen grid reliability by building more than $15 billion of reliable baseload power generation.

item.title: A New Rift in the Gulf, and Only the Gulf Can Solve It
item.description: Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates have a lot in common. Instead of fostering cooperation, it led to rivalry.

item.title: An “America First” Tech Stack Cannot Be America Alone
item.description: The administration has not yet revealed the details of the American AI Exports Program and how it will work. To successfully compete with China, it should include the entire tech stack, facilitate cooperation with trusted partners, and be backed by real resources.

item.title: From Fraud to the Frontlines: Scam Centers Caught in the Cambodia-Thailand Conflict
item.description: In December 2025, Thailand struck Cambodian casino and hotel complexes, which it says were scam centers being used by the military. Though contested, the strikes show how a border dispute and transnational crime have become intertwined.

item.title: New Executive Order Ties U.S. Critical Minerals Security to Global Partnerships
item.description: A new executive order makes international cooperation central to U.S. critical minerals security, targeting processed minerals where China dominates. It pairs allied supply agreements with trade tools—and potential price supports—to reduce vulnerabilities.

item.title: The Costs and Global Trade-Offs of U.S. Military Action Against Venezuela
item.description: U.S. military operations in the Caribbean, now in their sixth month, cost $31 million per day, $3 million of which is unbudgeted. The larger cost is the strategic trade-off in the allocation of military assets: Forces in the Caribbean are not available for other hotspots.
